# AI that acts in the world.

<p class="lede">We build AI agents that work inside real software and real machines, not chatbots beside them: music tools, simulators, robots, archives. They see the whole environment, act in it safely, and notice what changed. The first one we shipped, Sideman, gives Claude the whole of Ableton Live.</p>

::: {.layers}
::: {.layer .perceive}
<div class="eyebrow c-perceive">Layer one</div>
### Perceive
What the model can see decides what it can do. We build the senses: bridges into an application's object model, observers that report what a human did by hand, embeddings over an archive, simulators that expose true state.
:::
::: {.layer .reason}
<div class="eyebrow c-reason">Layer two</div>
### Reason
Grammars, skills and evaluation. We teach the model how a domain is shaped so it looks instead of guessing, and we measure coverage against the real system rather than claiming it.
:::
::: {.layer .act}
<div class="eyebrow c-act">Layer three</div>
### Act
Real writes with real undo, control loops that move a machine in simulation or in the world, and a guard before anything destructive. An agent that acts has to be safe to be wrong.
:::
:::

## What we offer

::: {.cards .grid-2}
::: {.card-s}
<div class="eyebrow">Open source</div>
### Sideman
An MCP server for Ableton Live 12 built on Live's own object model rather than a hand-written list of commands. Everything Live can do is in reach, and it notices what you do by hand.
<a class="card-link" href="sideman.html">About Sideman →</a>
:::
::: {.card-s}
<div class="eyebrow">Public</div>
### Pappus
A local-first notebook that teaches. The AI sees every cell above your question and answers with a hint or a small step. It never runs a cell, and by default it can't write files: running the code is your job. Built on Answer.AI's SolveIt method.
<a class="card-link" href="https://slegroux.github.io/pappus/">About Pappus →</a>
:::
::: {.card-s}
<div class="eyebrow">Course</div>
### A track, start to finish
Ten lessons that build one melodic house track from an empty Set, with Claude doing the work in Live. Told twice: once for musicians, once for programmers.
<a class="card-link" href="course.html">About the course →</a>
:::
::: {.card-s}
<div class="eyebrow">Services</div>
### Work with us
Build, advise or teach: agents inside music and creative tools, speech and audio ML, interactive art, robotics and simulation, research to product, and workshops.
<a class="card-link" href="services.html">What we take on →</a>
:::
:::

## Why Sisyphe

::: {.measure}
Sisyphus pushed the same rock up the same hill, forever. Skilled work has more of that than anyone admits: the fortieth track rename, the thousandth labelled frame, the sim run you relaunch because one parameter was wrong. It all has to be done, and none of it needs you.

We build the thing that pushes the rock. You keep the part that needs you: the taste, the judgment, the call.
:::

## Two decades of situated systems, one idea

::: {.measure}
Before Sideman there was a string quartet played by four people's brain signals, a room that composed music from how you moved through it, and an arena where robots drove the score. A policy driving a robot from what its camera sees is the same idea with a different actuator: a system that perceives what is happening and answers with an action.
:::
